'''Karl Stuart Nelson''' (born June 14, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Born and raised in [[DeKalb, Illinois]], Nelson played scholastically at [[DeKalb High School (Illinois)|DeKalb High School]], where he earned all-state honors in football, was a star pitcher for the baseball team, and lettered in basketball.<ref name="PFR1">{{cite web| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NelsKa20/gamelog/ |title=Karl Nelson Stats |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=June 3, 2024}}</ref><ref name="DDC 1989.12.14">{{cite news |newspaper=DeKalb (IL) Daily Chronicle |title=Karl Nelson announces retirement from pro football |date=December 14, 1989 |page=13 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-chronicle-karl-nelson-retireme/148615502/ |access-date=June 3, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>

He played [[college football|collegiately]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]].<ref name="NFL">{{cite web| url=https://www.nfl.com/players/karl-nelson/ |title=Karl Nelson Stats |website=NFL.com |access-date=June 3, 2024}}</ref> As a junior, Nelson was named second-team All-Big Eight by the [[Associated Press]] (AP) and as a senior was tabbed first-team.<ref name="1981 AP">{{cite news |newspaper=St. Louis Post-Dispatch |title=Associated Press All-Big Eight |date=November 25, 1981 |page=68 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/7236707/associated_press_allbig_eight/ |access-date=June 3, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref><ref name="1982 AP">{{cite news |newspaper=The Des Moines Register |title=1982 AP All-Big Eight team |date=November 24, 1982 |page=2S |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/7236960/1982_ap_allbig_ten_football_team/ |access-date=June 3, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref> Also as a senior, he was honored by the [[Newspaper Enterprise Association]] as a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].<ref name="NEA 1982">{{cite news |title=Hershel (sic) Walker and John Elway Head '82 NEA All America team |author=Murray Olderman |newspaper=The Albert Lea Tribune (MN) |date=December 26, 1982 |page=12 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-albert-lea-tribune-1982-nea-all-amer/147553231/ |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>

Nelson was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the third-round of the [[1983 NFL draft]].<ref name="PFR2">{{Cite web |title=1983 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1983/draft.htm |access-date=June 3, 2024 |website=Pro Football Reference}}</ref> He spent his rookie season on the [[injured reserve list]], but started all 55 games at right tackle over the next three seasons, culminating with the Giants victory in [[Super Bowl XXI]].<ref name="PFA">{{Cite web |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playern/nels04400.html |title=Karl Nelson Stats |website=Pro Football Archives |access-date=June 3, 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601160206/https://www.profootballarchives.com/playern/nels04400.html |archive-date=June 1, 2023}}</ref>

Shortly after the Super Bowl, Nelson was diagnosed with [[Hodgkin's disease]], and sat out the 1987 season. He made an amazing comeback in 1988, regaining his starting job, but injured his ankle in week 2. He returned from the injury in week 9, appearing in 7 more games that season. His Hodgkin's disease returned in 1989, forcing him to sit out yet another season, although he did help to coach the team's offensive line. He announced his retirement on December 13, 1989, saying, "I don't have the push for those five-hour workout days anymore."<ref name="PFR1"/><ref name="DDC 1989.12.14"/>

In 1989, Nelson was the recipient of the [[George Halas Award]], given by the [[Pro Football Writers of America]] (PFWA) to an NFL player, coach or staff member who overcomes the most adversity to succeed.<ref name="Halas">{{cite web |url=https://www.profootballwriters.org/off-field-awards/pfwa-george-halas-award/ |title=George Halas Award |publisher=Pro Football Writers of America |access-date=June 3, 2024}}</ref>

He also served as a commentator on Giants radio broadcasts.<ref name="DDC 1989.12.14"/>

Nelson went on to work in the financial services industry, and in 1993 published an autobiography, "Life on the Line".<ref name="DDC 1993.08.29">{{cite news |newspaper=DeKalb (IL) Daily Chronicle |title=Mark Vancil's Rare Air, Karl Nelson's story hit bookshelves |date=August 29, 1993 |page=11 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-chronicle-karl-nelson-book/148616452/ |access-date=June 3, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>

Nelson currently{{when|date=March 2019}} resides with his wife, Inga, in Northern New Jersey and is an active advocate for various charities. His primary charity is Adopt-a-Soldier Platoon.
